“Come What May” stands out as the only completely original song in Baz Luhrmann’s sprawling, mash-up jukebox musical Moulin Rouge!, but its origins actually predate the film. Songwriters David Baerwald and Kevin Gilbert originally composed the sweeping romantic ballad for Luhrmann’s previous project, the 1996 modern adaptation of Romeo + Juliet. Although it was cut from that film, Luhrmann resurrected it to serve as the secret love theme between Christian and Satine. However, this recycling came with a major critical cost: because the song was technically originally written for Romeo + Juliet and not explicitly conceived for Moulin Rouge!, the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences strictly disqualified it from being nominated for the Best Original Song Oscar, despite it being the movie’s signature track.

Moulin Rouge! (2001), directed by Baz Luhrmann, starring Nicole Kidman, Ewan McGregor, John Leguizamo, Jim Broadbent. In 1899 Paris, a young, idealistic English poet falls into a passionate but doomed secret romance with the star courtesan of the city’s most infamous and glamorous cabaret, sparking a dangerous love triangle with a ruthless, wealthy Duke.
